newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian firm launches Web search facility.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm launches Web search facility.

text.p: Malaysia's Alam Teknokrat Sdn Bhd said on Thursday that it and U.S. partner AltaVista Software Inc have launched an Internet search "mirror site" in Malaysia to serve Web page users in Asia.
The computer complex, south of Kuala Lumpur at Universiti Putra Malaysia in Serdang, is similar to AltaVista's main search facility at Palo Alto, California.
Internet services firm Alam Teknokrat will help to operate and manage the AltaVista Asia-Wide Mirror Site (http://altavista.skali.com.my).
The Malaysian-based facility will allow for quicker Web page searches, as the cyberspace queries will be routed within Asia rather than sent to the United States.
"This service will provide dramatic performance advantages to millions of Internet users in Asia," Alam Teknokrat said in a statement released at the Internet Society's annual convention.

Hisham Isa, chief executive oficer at Alam Teknokrat, said in a speech at the product launch: "The establishment of this Asian mirror site signifies our commitment to facilitating and developing the growth and use of the Internet in Asia."

Alam Teknokrat on Thursday also signed an Internet news service agreement with Malaysian government-owned Bernama news agency under which the media group will provide news breaks and news update summaries to its Web site.
The mirror site uses high-end Digital Equipment Corp AlphaServers and is equipped with fibre optic cables linked to the Internet.

Alam Teknokrat said its mirror site could handle up to 1.2 million search requests a day, and that 150,000 search requests per day from Asia were currently being handled by AltaVista in the United States.
